questions.text: Covid-19, ___________, and tetanus are commonly recommended immunizations for health care providers.
Early recognition of foreign body airway obstruction is the ________ to successful outcome.
It is important to maintain the hand and foot of an injured extremity in a normal and comfortable position during _____________; this position is called the position of function.
Your patient has burned his hand, the skin is red and blistered and the burn is extremely painful; this burn would be classified as _________ thickness.
The ______ common vital signs are pulse, respirations, blood pressure, pupils, and skin signs.
Before ___________ a combative patient, the Emergency Medical Responder should obtain law enforcement assistance.
The _________ are found in an area behind the abdominal wall.
A patient has been involved in a rollover vehicle collision; in this __________, the rollover is an example of the mechanism of injury.
On the lower half of the sternum is the most appropriate hand location for chest compressions on an _______.
You have responded to a call for a possible overdose; you should first _______ that the scene is safe.
You have just finished applying a splint to a patient's leg; you should __________ circulation, sensation, and motor function.
Hypoxia from _________ respirations is a potential complication from a patient who appears to have injured a rib without a flailed segment, and the patient is alert and oriented.
The appropriate care for an amputated body part is to wrap it with ______ gauze and place it on ice.
Immediate transport is the most important to the survival of a patient showing ________ of shock.
When assessing a patient with a musculoskeletal injury, it is important to ________ circulation, sensation, and motor function.
